lines.4: 「Yes. The house is clean, and I was already quite willing to live here, so I am glad.」
lines.5: 「I had been certain you would refuse.」
lines.6: 「I still don't really understand any of this, but maybe living together will help me see something I couldn't before.」
lines.8: 「But I don't want a repeat of what just happened.」
lines.9: 「I did not come here to pick a fight. Since we are to live together, I hope we can get along.」
lines.10: 「But when I believe you are in the wrong, I will still scold you.」
lines.12: 「Then I look forward to living with you.」
lines.13: 「We got along well when we were young. I am sure we can do so now.」
lines.14: To be honest, there was one thing I could never say out loud.
lines.15: Here I was, under one roof with a woman who easily ranked among the three most beautiful at my school.
lines.16: That couldn't help making me a little happy.
lines.17: It was part of the reason I accepted.
lines.19: 「What is it? Do you have another question?」
lines.20: 「What should I call you? Or, uh, what should I call you, ma'am?」
lines.21: 「There is no need for formal speech.」
lines.22: 「This is your home. You should be more at ease.」
lines.23: That was a relief to hear.
lines.24: A foreign presence was entering the territory where I had always lived alone.
lines.25: Even though Crab and Subaru had gotten me used to company, I still felt considerable resistance to that part of it.
lines.26: 「So, just as when we were children, you may think of me as an older sister.」
lines.28: 「As for what to call me, I would prefer Otome-nee-san or Otome-san.」
lines.29: 「A surname would be too distant for two people living together.」
lines.31: 「What is wrong? That answer lacked conviction.」
lines.33: 「Yes. That is how a proper answer should sound.」
lines.34: She was completely back to her usual self.
